az_black_roof.blurb: Black Roof is a small roof-bouldering sector in Priest Draw, outside Flagstaff in northern Arizona. It has six problems, all boulders, running from the middle of the V5 range up to V12, so it suits strong climbers more than beginners. The roof is blackened with old campfire soot and has one clear left-to-right line of weakness that holds the hard problems, which rely on powerful pulls on very small holds. An easier problem sits on the roof's left side. The walk is only a couple of minutes up the draw from the main parking area, with the roof right beside the trail.

az_cove_wall_the.blurb: The Cove Wall is a bouldering wall in the compact Stone Cove, in the Lake Mary area near Flagstaff, at roughly 7,000 feet. It holds six problems between V2 and V4: a bulging wall where awkward starts lead into dynamic moves over the lip. A big hollow flake sits at the steepest point and is not trustworthy. Expect problems that feel harder than their grades. The Cove makes a good early-season training spot. To get there, follow the trail up the gully and the wall appears on your right.

az_h_the_half_life_wall.blurb: The Half-life Wall is a short bouldering wall along the Drysdale Trail at The Ridge, near Lower Lake Mary south of Flagstaff, at about 7,000 feet. It has six problems on bulging terrain, mostly easy to moderate, from the lowest grades up through V2, with a single harder problem near V5. That makes it a popular place to warm up. Walking east along the trail, you pass the Booze Pig Wall first, and this is the next wall along. The trail strings together about half a mile of walls, with views over the lake toward Mormon Mountain.
